summary: The root دَسَسَ (dassasa) primarily means to conceal, hide, or bury something, often implying a surreptitious or deceptive act.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: دَسَّهُ س , (S, M, A, &c.,) aor. دَسُسَ , (M, Msb,) inf. n. دَسٌّ (M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and دَسِّيسَى , (K,) like خِصِّيصَى , (TA,) He hid it, or concealed it, (Lth, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) namely, anything, (A, Mgh, Msb,) in the earth or dust, (S, Mgh,) or beneath a thing: (A, Mgh:) he buried it (A, Msb, K) in the earth or dust, (Msb,) or beneath a thing: (K:) or he put it in, or inserted it, beneath: (M:) or, accord. to some, he put it in, or inserted it, with force; he thrust it in: (TA:) and and , (M, K, *) in the latter of which one of the س is changed into ى because the reduplication is disliked, (M, * TA,) signify the same as دَسَّهُ , (M, K, *) [or, probably, have an intensive signification.] It is said in the Kur [xvi. 61],

parts.t: in the earth or dust, or beneath a thing:
Such a one came secretly to such a one, bringing him calumnies
he came to such a one with calumnies.

headwords.def: اندسّ دس دسه دسة [ He, or it, became hidden, or concealed, in the earth or dust, or beneath a thing: he, or it, hid, or concealed, himself, or itself, in the earth &c.:] he, or it, became buried: he, or it, buried himself, or itself: (S, K:) or it became put in, or inserted, or it put in, or inserted, itself, beneath. (M.) [Hence,] اندسّ فُلَانٌ إِلَى فُلَانٍ يَأْتِيهِ بِالنَّمَائِمِ (tropical:) [ Such a one came secretly to such a one, bringing him calumnies ]: (TA:) or اندسّ الى فلان means (assumed tropical:) he came to such a one with calumnies. (Ham p. 219.)

headwords.gloss: concealment of guile; artifice; One whom thou hidest

parts.t: in order that he may bring thee news,
one whom a people send secretly to bring them news,
the spy of a people, who searches for, and then brings, news,
Persons hypocritical in their actions, who enter among the reciters of the Kur-án when they are not of them.

headwords.def: دَسِيسٌ دسيس The concealment of guile or artifice. (S.) One whom thou hidest, or concealest, ( مَنْ تَدُسُّهُ ,) in order that he may bring thee news, or information: (M, K:) accord. to some, similar to مُتَحَسِّسٌ ; (M;) or مُتَجَسِّسٌ ; and called by the vulgar : (TA:) or دَسِيسُ قَوْمٍ signifies one whom a people send secretly to bring them news, or information; (A;) the spy of a people, who searches for, and then brings, news, or information; syn. جَاسُوس . (Msb.) And دُسُسٌ [pl. of دَسِيسٌ ] Persons hypocritical in their actions, who enter among the reciters of the Kur-án when they are not of them. (IAar, K.)

headwords.gloss: coming secretly to a person, bringing him calumnies; a secret machination; the like

parts.t: coming secretly to a person, bringing him calumnies:

headwords.def: دَسِيسَةٌ دسيسه دسيسة [app. The coming secretly to a person, bringing him calumnies: in modern Arabic, a secret machination or the like ]. (TA, where, after the phrase اندسّ فلان الى فلان يأتيه بالنمائم , (see 7,) it is added, وَهِىَّ الدَّسِيسَةٌ .)
